transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-05 15:30 UTC | Duration: 52 minutes | Recording: yes
Attendees: Evan (Redwood AE), Sofia (Redwood SE), Marcus (Redwood CSM), Priya (Aurelia Head ML), Derek (Aurelia Platform), Olivia (Aurelia InfoSec), Tom (Aurelia DevOps)

Summary block (auto-gen, may be rough):
- Quick status: credentials mostly in progress, small delay on KMS handshake due to compliance review.
- Benchmarks: p95 latency improved after prefix caching but cost bumped slightly.
- Decision: run canary on dedicated capacity for latency-sensitive routes; keep fallback to hosted.

[00:00] Evan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we'll give folks one more minute to pop in. So agenda is creds, staging gateway handoff, bench recap, and then plan for canary.
[00:35] Priya: Hi all, good to be here. Quick note, we've got a change in the security review timeline, which might push some KMS tests by a couple of days.
[00:44] Olivia: yeah, sorry, it's just that our third-party risk team flagged the HSM vendor, they're asking for certs. We're working it.
[00:52] Evan: Understood. Sofia, do you want to run through the bench highlights from last week's run?
[01:05] Sofia: Sure. So we ran the 10k prompt pass and then a follow-on 50k subset that Priya sent — couple of transcriptions here, some of the proper nouns in the logs got munged so we'll attach raw traces. The big win was prefix/KV cache warmup; median token latency dropped about 12-15% once KV was primed. p95 was down from 430ms to 360ms on Dedicated with our batching combo.
[01:40] Derek: Wait, 360ms p95 on Dedicated? That's pretty good — what GPU profile were you using?
[01:47] Sofia: It's a T4-equivalent cluster with our quantized runtime, so not full FP16 V100-class. The quantization profile for this workload was q4_0 with some kernel-level tuning — that gave us better memory density, small cost win.
[02:05] Priya: Are there any hallucination/regression checks tied to quantization? We can't sacrifice quality.
[02:12] Sofia: Great question. We ran the eval harness against the same prompt set; delta in rouge/f1 was within the tolerance they approved, but we'll attach the detailed eval. There were a few edge-cases in domain-specific entity recognition — we'll add those to the regression prompt set.
[02:33] Tom: From ops side, I'm worried about cold-starts for the KV cache across pods; how are you priming on scale-up?
[02:40] Marcus: We have a background priming job for active prefixes and a progressive rollout so that pods prefetch most-requested keys. It does mean a small burst of network IO during scale events.
[02:55] Tom: ok that helps. How about autoscaler settings; our burst profiles are kinda spiky.
[03:05] Sofia: We recommend an aggressive warmup window plus burst capacity on Dedicated for those spikes. For hosted routes, we keep lower concurrency but faster spin-up; tradeoff is cost.
[03:20] Priya: Speaking of cost, what's the delta if we do 10% canary on Dedicated vs all-hosted?
[03:27] Evan: Roughly, 10% on Dedicated increases committed cost by about 8% but reduces p95 latency by ~20ms in our model for that route. We'll send the updated cost comp in the deck.
[03:40] Olivia: Back to security, the KMS handshake — are you guys supporting our HSM's PKCS interface or only cloud KMS?
[03:47] Sofia: We support both but the HSM flow requires a bit more ops work and an offline key injection step. We can do an initial CI smoke with cloud KMS while the HSM certs are cleared.
[04:02] Olivia: That sounds fine but we need rotation logs, audit trail and proof of key usage for SOC2.
[04:10] Evan: We can export audit logs and key usage events; Marcus will coordinate the retention window options.
[04:18] Marcus: Yep I'll follow up.
[04:22] [small crosstalk] Priya: there's also an ask from product — they want per-route latency SLO of p95 < 300ms for the search route. Are we on track?
[04:31] Sofia: We're close on Dedicated with priming and quantization; on hosted we usually sit at ~340ms p95 for same workload. Hitting 300ms will require heavier batching optimizations or a larger GPU profile.
[04:45] Derek: Could we do hybrid: Dedicated for search, hosted for other routes?
[04:50] Evan: Yes, that's exactly the smart routing approach — you can pin routes to Dedicated and fallback to hosted if capacity is exhausted.
[04:58] Tom: Any network egress concerns if we use Dedicated in a different region?
[05:03] Sofia: That's why we recommend colocating Dedicated in the same cloud region as staging. If not possible, latency will increase due to cross-region hops; we can quantify that.
[05:15] [06:00] Priya: ok, about staging gateway handoff — Derek, what do you need from Redwood to finish the proxy config?
[06:05] Derek: I need the exact endpoint, cert thumbprint, and the header schema for tracing. Also, rate-limits and retry policy so we can mirror production behavior.
[06:16] Evan: We'll provide a stubbed config and cert thumbprint. Marcus — can your team share the header schema?
[06:22] Marcus: I'll put that in the shared drive after the call.
[06:26] Derek: Great.
[06:30] [07:10] Olivia: On SCIM/SAML, we have a bunch of attributes we require for user provisioning. Are you supporting SCIM v2?
[07:18] Evan: Yes, SCIM v2 for provisioning, and SAML for SSO. We'll need the metadata file. If you can send it, we'll spin up a test SSO.
[07:26] Olivia: I'll send it after we confirm the required claim mapping.
[07:30] Priya: There was also a note about data residency — some prompts contain PHI; will logs be redacted?
[07:38] Sofia: We can enable PII redaction and token-level retention settings per project. For PHI, we recommend Private deployment or VPC deployment with customer-managed KMS.
[07:48] Priya: Ok we'll treat that as must-have for any production move.
[07:52] [08:20] Derek: small question — when you talk about quantization profile q4_0, is that the one we tested in the previous run or different?
[08:27] Sofia: Same profile. There's an alternate q8_0 that ups quality but uses more memory; tradeoff is fewer concurrent contexts.
[08:36] Evan: Maybe for the search route we pick q8_0 on Dedicated to reach the 300ms target, and keep q4_0 for bulk generation.
[08:45] Priya: Let's mark that as an experiment.
[08:48] [09:00] Tom: About gateway TLS certs — can Redwood accept Let's Encrypt style certs or do you need our enterprise CA?
[09:08] Evan: We accept both but for Private deployments enterprise CA is preferred. For staging Let's Encrypt is fine.
[09:12] Tom: ok.
[09:15] [10:00] Priya: I want to clarify timeline: HSM certs are likely cleared by Monday next week, so KMS full integration could be mid-week. That shifts our earlier go/no-go a little.
[10:25] Olivia: yes, and once HSM is in we'll need to verify rotation policy in a test run.
[10:32] Marcus: We'll prepare a rotation test that simulates key rollover.
[10:38] Evan: Good.
[10:40] [12:00] Sofia: On the benchmark details — two quick notes: 1) the dataset Priya gave has a heavy tail of long prompts which inflate tail latencies; 2) prefix caching effectiveness depends on prompt re-use — the test set was modestly representative but we'll need production traces to fully tune.
[12:22] Priya: We'll push larger traces next couple days.
[12:28] Derek: Also, what about telemetry — we want token-level cost breakdowns per route. Is that available?
[12:36] Marcus: Yes, Redwood Console exposes token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route and model; we can map project keys to route dashboards.
[12:43] Derek: Great, that's helpful for our FinOps folks.
[12:47] [15:00] Evan: Let's cover the staging handoff checklist: credentials, certs, routing, SSO, header schema, bench traces, and the KMS smoke test. Anything missing?
[15:12] Tom: Add the canary routing config and the fallback policy to the checklist.
[15:18] Priya: And the regression prompt set for quantization edge-cases.
[15:22] Evan: Perfect. We'll annotate owner for each item.
[15:26] [20:00] Sofia: Quick note on fallbacks — we can configure automatic fallback to a hosted-compatible model variant if Dedicated capacity spikes beyond threshold. That keeps the app online but might increase latency slightly.
[20:16] Priya: What's the impact on session continuity for chat flows when fallback occurs?
[20:22] Sofia: If you use the same model family and maintain KV cache semantics, session continuity is preserved; but if fallback changes quantization or model size, there can be small differences in tokenization and response structure. We log those events for audit.
[20:38] Priya: Good to know.
[20:42] [25:00] Derek: ops question — will we get an allowlist of IPs for the staging gateway so our firewall team can pre-approve?
[25:09] Evan: Yes, we'll provide IP ranges and the cert thumbprint.
[25:15] Tom: Also need a maintenance window for the priming job to avoid noisy neighbor effects.
[25:23] Marcus: We'll coordinate with you to pick low-traffic windows.
[25:27] [30:00] Priya: can we talk about SLO measurement — how do you recommend measuring p95 for our search route?
[30:09] Sofia: Use end-to-end synthetic probes with representative payloads, and correlate with token-level metrics from the console. For production, sample traces and compute p95 over 5-minute windows, track regressions via the eval hooks.
[30:23] Priya: ok we'll set up a dashboard.
[30:27] [35:00] Evan: All right, let's capture concrete owners:
[35:10] Evan: Priya - share 50k test set and traces; Olivia - SAML metadata; Derek - cert thumbprint + header schema; Marcus - schedule on-prem ops walkthrough; Evan - pricing and cost comp; Sofia - attach detailed eval and bench logs.
[35:34] Priya: will do.
[35:37] Olivia: will send the SAML metadata this afternoon.
[35:41] Derek: we'll push traces by Friday.
[35:44] Marcus: I'll set a calendar invite for the ops walkthrough.
[35:47] Evan: ok final quick Qs?
[35:50] Tom: None from me.
[35:53] Priya: Nope.
[35:55] Evan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up in writing and circulate the checklist and action items.
[36:02] [Closeout] Evan: Meeting adjourned.

Notes and attachments referenced: shared drive link to bench traces (drive.redwood.com/aurelia/pilot/bench-0504), evaluation report (redwood-evals/quantization-q4_0-vs-q8_0.pdf), pilot-pricing-v2.xlsx.

- Evan to send pricing comp and dedicated burst option by 2027-05-07.
- Olivia to send SAML/SCIM metadata and security attribute mapping by 2027-05-10.
